pr_body:
Fixes [#12314](https://github.com/netdata/netdata/issues/12314)

<!--
Describe the change in summary section, including rationale and design decisions.
Include "Fixes #nnn" if you are fixing an existing issue.

In "Test Plan" provide enough detail on how you plan to test this PR so that a reviewer can validate your tests. If our CI covers sufficient tests, then state which tests cover the change.

If you have more information you want to add, write them in "Additional
Information" section. This is usually used to help others understand your
motivation behind this change. A step-by-step reproduction of the problem is
helpful if there is no related issue.
-->

##### Summary
Issue:
The query returns slate data when a chart becomes invalid due to several reasons such as;
removed USB disk or stopped application services.

Root Problem:
"Before" parameter is set relatively to the "last_entry_t".

Solution:
"Before" parameter is set relatively to the "now_realtime_sec()".
"last_entry_t" checks/conditions are removed.

##### Test Plan
Expected behavior
When we ask data for the last 10 minutes, the duration of the data returned should be of the last 10 minutes, independently of the whether the chart stopped being collected.

Steps to reproduce:
- Start a container
- Wait a few minutes for netdata to gather some data
- Stop the container
- Wait a few minutes
- refresh the agent dashboard
- the container charts do not have a gap at the end of the chart. They feel "recent".
<!---
Provide enough detail so that your reviewer can understand which test-cases you
have covered, and recreate them if necessary. If sufficient tests are covered
by our CI, then state which tests cover the change.
-->

##### Additional Information
Fix is tested with steps below:
- First we need a chart which can be disabled easily to reproduce the issue, I used a USB disk.
- Plugin the USB disk to the machine which runs netdata agent and wait one minute to get metrics of `disk_busy.sdb`
- Check the metrics with `http://127.0.0.1:19999/api/v1/data?chart=disk_busy.sdb&after=-10&options=jsonwrap` request on the browser. Don't forget to change `sdb `with your USB disk name.
- Then remove the USB disk and wait 20-30 seconds.
- When you call the same request, it responds with the last 10 metrics of USB disk. But expected output is "`NULL`" because it does not get the metrics for last 20-30 seconds.
- This PR enables creating of response relative to the time of request not the last metric store time.

Actually these steps are taken from the bug, let me explain it in a detailed way.

First we need a chart which can be disabled easily to reproduce the issue, I used a USB disk.
Plugin the USB disk to the machine which runs netdata agent and wait one minute to get metrics of `disk_busy.sdb`
Check the metrics with `http://127.0.0.1:19999/api/v1/data?chart=disk_busy.sdb&after=-10&options=jsonwrap` request on the browser. Don't forget to change `sdb` with your USB disk name.
Then remove the USB disk and wait 20-30 seconds.
When you call the same request, it responds with the last 10 metrics of USB disk, because _**it feels it the most recent values :)**_ . But expected output is "NULL" because it does not get the metrics for last 20-30 seconds.
This PR enables creating of response relative to the time of request not the last metric store time.

There is an issue when memory mode is RAM or SAVE

- Start parent with memory mode RAM or SAVE and child
- Check the `http://127.0.0.1:19999/host/CHILD/api/v1/data?chart=system.cpu&after=-10&options=jsonwrap`
   - Keep refreshing for at least 10 seconds to observe data collecting
   - Stop child and notice null values as expected (keep refreshing)
     - After 10 seconds notice that the 10th value is not null but the last value collected for the chart

> @erdem2000 any progress?

Due to replication GAP mechanism optimization task, I plan to fix it on Friday latest.

Sorry for the late return. The last commit also fixes stationary metric output with `ram ` and `save ` memory modes.

We should also investigate the behavior below & if it is necessary open another issue for it.
When investigating the reason of this issue (with `ram `memory mode) I also figured out that `[rd->state->query_ops.next_metric(&handle, &db_now);](https://github.com/netdata/netdata/blob/b0e6c0700e6ea9615d9b2f4d4352ec8ea965eb05/web/api/queries/query.c#L593)` function returns the storage number with the `SN_ANOMALY_BIT` at the first call. 
Because of that `[does_storage_number_exist(n)](https://github.com/netdata/netdata/blob/b0e6c0700e6ea9615d9b2f4d4352ec8ea965eb05/web/api/queries/query.c#L602)` check returns `true ` and the metric is evaluated as a number instead of `null`.

If this behavior is fixed then we can revoke the related part of the PR.

issue_context.title: [Bug]: Relative queries return old data
issue_context.body:
### Bug description

When we call `/api/v1/data` with a relative timeframe (e.g. `before=0` and `after=-600` to show the last 10 minutes), the agent responds with the relative timeframe against the last time a chart was collected.

This means that:

1. for charts that are currently being collected, the agent responds with the last 10 minutes.
2. for charts that are no longer being collected, the agent responds with 10 minutes of data, relative to the time the chart was last collected.

This makes things on the dashboard very confusing. Charts are not always aligned and if a chart failed to be updated recently the user accidentally sees stale data on the charts (the x-axis is right, but still the user needs to pay attention to notice it).

### Expected behavior

When we ask data for the last 10 minutes, the duration of the data returned should be of the last 10 minutes, independently of the whether the chart stopped being collected.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start a container
2. Wait a few minutes for netdata to gather some data
3. Stop the container
4. Wait a few minutes
5. refresh the agent dashboard
6. the container charts do not have a gap at the end of the chart. They feel "recent".


### Installation method

kickstart.sh

### System info

```shell
N/A
```


### Netdata build info

```shell
N/A
```


### Additional info

_No response_
